_contract: The MECHANISM's instance facts for a baseline-completion authorization: which contract, which field split, where the money block is, and the project cap the arithmetic checks against. AUTHORIZES NOTHING.
_what_is_deliberately_absent: the ceiling, the expected cost, the price basis, the plan hash, the B identities and the frozen candidate identity. Every one of those has a canonical owner -- the completion pricing record, the completion protocol, the baseline construction and the frozen candidate record -- and the issuer DERIVES each from its owner. Restating any here would create a second place to edit and a way for the two to disagree. In particular Search-1's accepted $15.0446 pricing is NOT reused: it prices a ten-hour beam and authorizes nothing here.
_stage_id_meaning: the stage of the overall project this run belongs to, which is the same Stage 1 initialization work Search-1 belongs to. It is the run-layout stage, not a driver stage.
_authorized_stages_meaning: the completion driver's two stages. Stage A binds every shared identity and loads nothing; stage B rebuilds B once, measures it once and computes the comparison. There is no third stage and no beam.

grant_contract._field_split: STATED is what only a person can say. The identities block is the other half: a grant records what the maintainer approved against and the issuer RE-DERIVES every one of them, refusing on any disagreement. An identity the issuer does not know how to derive is itself a refusal, so a grant cannot introduce a binding nobody checks.

money._why: the generic cap arithmetic in src/aadistill/governance/grant.py takes a FLAT mapping with configurable field names; a grant records the project's position in one nested block. The block is named here and flattened by the assembler, so the arithmetic still happens in exactly one place.

grant_contract._no_reviewed_commit: no verified-identity field names a commit. The issuer's HEAD is necessarily LATER than the grant -- the grant is committed, then the readiness sweep runs on that clean tree, then the record is committed, and only then is the authorization issued -- so a grant that predicted the issuance commit would make its own chain unsatisfiable. C1 attempt 15 aborted on exactly that.

accepted_pricing._why_only_the_cap: the cap is a PROJECT fact the grant arithmetic checks a ceiling against, and it is not derivable from this session's own pricing. The ceiling, the expected cost and the price basis all come from the completion pricing record.

stage_conditions.bind_identities: loads no model and measures nothing. Binds the frozen Search-1 run id and config hash, the selection commitment, the suite hash, the policy hash and its epsilon, the teacher revision, the frozen B construction and the evaluator's own source hashes. A disagreement here is a STOP, not something to compensate for.
stage_conditions.rebuild_measure_compare: rebuilds the frozen B ONCE through its complete deterministic fixed path, measures it ONCE on the frozen state_eval suite with the evaluator primed by that same original teacher object, and computes the preregistered B->C comparison against the five frozen candidate measurements. No beam, no new candidate, no candidate remeasured.

_stage_conditions_meaning: what each authorized stage may do. Carried into the authorization so a reader of the artifact sees the boundary without opening the protocol.
